slot_note: wave 6, Opportunity Sizing block; seed OS07 (the world, the decision and the quantity only: a regional grocer opening one of six shortlisted sites next year, sized by its incremental annual contribution)
niche: which shortlisted site a regional grocery chain opens next year, sized by a spend-share (Huff) model whose origins are census output areas, when one site is the nearest of the six to a 1,750-pitch holiday park whose guests live outside the region
answer: S3 Wrentoft, Mill Lane, adding GBP 0.8 million a year to the chain's contribution
answer_source: golden workbook and submission.md, from generator/figures.json
analyst_test: A strong analyst runs the filed spend-share model over the census output areas' household grocery spend, adds each site to the 24 grocery stores of 280 m2 or more on the rating list, nets what it takes from our ten stores, confirms the model against the estate's sales (ratio 1.00) and the card feed, and approves S1 Bellingtoft at GBP 0.5 million, because the census output areas are not every origin of grocery spend: the guests on Wrentoft Lakes Holiday Park's 1,750 pitches live outside the region.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a new store's trade from the retail geographer's spatial-interaction model, every origin's grocery spend shared among the stores by floor area and distance deterrence; a holiday park is an origin the census never counts, and its guests' spend is priced per pitch from the out-of-region cardholders at the chain's stores beside other parks, so swapping in a hospital's patients or a utility's megawatt-hours loses the census origin set, the park pitches on the rating list and the acquirer's home-sector feed that measure the guests.
layer1: Census 2021 output areas with population-weighted centroids on the British National Grid
ONS Postcode Directory extract with terminated postcodes and their termination months
VOA non-domestic rating list in its own descriptions, with the summary valuation's main measure in m2, parking spaces or pitches
a payment acquirer's merchant-insight feed of card spend by month and cardholder home postcode sector, out-of-region sectors included
modelled grocery spend per household by output area from a data provider
the chain's financial year (April to March) against calendar-month feeds
stakeholder_role: the chain's finance director, who chairs the property committee

spine.entity: one hereditament on the non-domestic rating list in the planning region

world.geography: England (a planning region of twelve towns and sixty-one rural parishes on the British National Grid, postcode area LQ)

driver: The demand model's origins are the resident count, and a body of short-stay occupants counted at homes outside the area sits in no origin; their spend, measured at existing outlets beside similar lodgings and priced per lodging unit, decides which candidate adds most.
driver_concrete: The spend-share model's origins are the census output areas, and Wrentoft Lakes Holiday Park's 1,750 pitches hold guests who live outside the region; their grocery spend, priced per pitch from the out-of-region cardholders at our stores beside Raddleford Water and Withybeck Lakes, makes S3 Wrentoft the site that adds most.
stump: A competent analyst runs the filed spend-share model over the census households' spend, finds it reproduces the estate's sales and approves S1 Bellingtoft at GBP 0.5 million where the golden is S3 Wrentoft at GBP 0.8 million; the step that lands them there is taking the census output areas as every origin of grocery spend, when the guests on Wrentoft Lakes Holiday Park's 1,750 pitches live outside the region.

differentiation.task199: task199's record holds an event only where a watcher filed it, so a unit's rise is read against its own filing volume; here no record depends on a watcher: the census is complete for the region's residents, and the missing origin is a holiday park's guests, who appear in no count and are priced per pitch from the out-of-region cardholders the acquirer's feed shows at the chain's stores beside other parks.
differentiation.task268: task268's first architecture carried people present at small areas from a commuting table at a survey's on-site rate, and its later ones a stock retreating from collectors and survival through lost follow-up; here the missing people are holiday guests who live outside the region, absent from every table in the pack, whose only measure is the grocery spend per pitch that out-of-region cardholders leave at stores beside other parks.
differentiation.task133: task133's loan record never watched the months before a system takeover, a left truncation of exposure in a unit-level record; here nothing is truncated or unwatched: the census is complete for its residents and the gap is an origin of spend it never holds.
differentiation.task180: task180's catalogue masks small events in the noisy hours of a daily cycle, a detection gap inside one record; here no event goes undetected: the census counts residents correctly and the decisive origin, a holiday park's guests, is outside its scope altogether.
differentiation.task196: task196 recovers how many events a record only partly captures from the overlap of two capture channels; here nothing is under-captured, since the census is complete for the residents it counts, and the missing origin is a body of non-resident guests priced per pitch from the seasonal out-of-region card spend at the chain's own stores.
differentiation.task255: task255 reads the upper tail of a size distribution truncated at item-specific floors and capped by a moving ceiling; here no item is truncated or censored, and the decisive step is the spend-share model's origin set, which leaves out a population the census never counts.
differentiation.task271: task271 corrects a risk estimate for clusters that reached the record through an affected member; here no unit enters any file through its outcome, and the guests are absent from the census by where they live, not by selection on what they spend.
differentiation.task273: task273 infers each group's exposure from the uninvolved parties of two-party events drawn where events are frequent; here the omitted demand is measured directly, the guests' card spend in season at the chain's stores, and priced per pitch over the parks that send it.
differentiation.task456: task456 estimates how often a state holds from three records that each misclassify; here every record reads as what it is, and the call turns on which places the demand model takes spend to start from.
differentiation.task462: task462 totals intermittent sources seen only by snapshot surveys whose detection rises with size; here the omitted demand is not missed by a survey but never counted by the census, and the card feed measures it month by month.

notes: Shape other: the call is one of six sites with its addition to the chain's annual contribution (2 criteria plus its components), and the asks grade the existing estate and the six sites on measures the call does not turn on (26 figures: DC cases a week by store, paid hours a week by store, bus departures by site on a Friday); grading every site's addition would pay the resident route five of six. Probes before the draw (2026-10-24, call-only, isolated, medium): sonnet and opus both approved the site now named S1 Bellingtoft; opus refitted the model to the card feed, called the out-of-region cardholders 1.7 per cent of card spend and read the park-side store's end-of-season fall as competition.
